partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia, X-linked, due to factor 8 defect
partners.mechanism_chain: Pathogenic variant in F8 (MONDO:0010602) —DISRUPTS→ F8 (HGNC:3546); Pathogenic variant in F8 (MONDO:0859082) —DISRUPTS→ F8 (HGNC:3546); F8 (HGNC:3546) —DECREASES→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-600002); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-600002) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding diathesis (HP:0001871); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-600002) —LEADS_TO→ Increased risk of thrombosis (HP:0001383). partners.diseaseBName: congenital disorder of glycosylation, type IIaa
partners.mechanism_chain: F8 (HGNC:3788) —DISRUPTS→ Factor VIII secretion (GO:0007275); Factor VIII secretion (GO:0007275) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding (HP:0001871); STX5 (HGNC:11140) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794); Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794) —DISRUPTS→ Protein N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486); Protein N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation, type IIaa (MONDO:0957540). Loss-of-function mutations in F8 impair the secretion of functional Factor VIII, leading to Hemophilia A. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in STX5 disrupt the normal functioning of the Golgi apparatus, which is critical for protein N-linked glycosylation, resulting in CDG-IIaa. The convergence is on the Golgi apparatus and the general process of protein glycosylation, which is essential for the proper function and secretion of many proteins, including Factor VIII.

partners.mechanism_chain: F8 (HGNC:3790) —DISRUPTS→ coagulation cascade (GO:0007596); coagulation cascade (GO:0007596) —LEADS_TO→ bleeding tendency (HP:0001874); CTSC (HGNC:2509) —DISRUPTS→ extracellular matrix degradation (GO:0009251); extracellular matrix degradation (GO:0009251) —LEADS_TO→ periodontitis (HP:0000764); extracellular matrix degradation (GO:0009251) —LEADS_TO→ palmoplantar hyperkeratosis (HP:0000970); extracellular matrix degradation (GO:0009251) —LEADS_TO→ short stature (HP:0004325). Loss-of-function mutations in F8 disrupt the coagulation cascade, leading to a bleeding tendency (hemophilia A). Loss-of-function mutations in CTSC impair extracellular matrix degradation, contributing to phenotypes like periodontitis, hyperkeratosis, and short stature seen in Haim-Munk syndrome. The convergence is on the broader biological process of extracellular matrix regulation, where impaired clotting (hemophilia A) affects vascular integrity and repair, and impaired ECM degradation (Haim-Munk syndrome) directly affects tissue structure and turnover. Both pathways, though distinct in their primary molecular players, impinge on the maintenance and integrity of tissues, including the vasculature and skin, which share common ECM components and remodeling processes.
